p:cNvPr.descr: The diagram begins with RNA, labeled at the left. The chain begins with a phosphate group. O- bonds down to P, which bonds left to O-, double bonds right to O, and down to O. O bonds down to CH2, which is labeled at right with a small 5'. The CH2 marks the beginning of the pentose ring which repeats down the chain. CH2 bonds down to C, which bonds down to H and down & left to C. C bonds up to H and down to O, which is part of the next phosphodiester bond. Next to this there is a small 3'. C bonds right to C, which bonds up and down to H and up and right to C. C bonds up to box labeled base 1, down to H, and up and right to O, which bonds down and left to the C that began the chain. This constitutes a single pentose ring. The O bonds down to the next phosphate group, and the chain repeats again, but now the pentose ring is bonded to a box labeled base 2. A partial phosphate group is shown below as a continuation of the RNA strand. To the right of the RNA, there is an OH- that transfers electrons to the H on the pentose ring, shown by a red arrow.The O-H bond then transfers electrons to the P in the phosphate group. Electrons then transfer from P down to the bottom O in phosphate. A right arrow indicates moving on to the hydrolyzed RNA. The RNA has split at the bottom O of the center phosphate group. The top molecule is labeled to the left 2',3'-monophosphate derivative, and it consists of a pentose ring, bonded right to a box labeled base 1, bonded up and down to a phosphate group. A right arrow labeled H2O from this group points to text reading, "mixture of 2' and 3' monophosphate derivatives." Below this image is a + sign. The image below the + sign is labeled to the left "shortened RNA." It consists of the bottom pentose ring bonded to the right to a box reading "base 2"; it bonds up on the left to CH2, which bonds up to O. The pentose ring then bonds down to an O on a partial phosphate group, bonded to only 3 oxygens.
